messages:
Anya: Heads-up — we've had a cluster of short GPU node flares in us-west over the last 6h. Alerts are firing every few minutes and waking oncall. Thinking we should try a probabilistic suppression + a short quieter-burst policy instead of immediate paging. Any objections?
Rob: Saw it. Agree we need something better. Can we make suppression dependent on sustained signal vs single-sample spikes? don't want to hide actual failures.
sre-bot: alert: gpu_node_flare fired (region=us-west-2) nodes=[vm-123, vm-456] severity=warning
Anya: Proposal sketch: replace the single hard threshold with a two-stage rule:
  - ticket immediately if sustained for >= 5m OR affected_nodes_count >= 3
  - otherwise, for first 3m use probabilistic paging (P(page)=10%), escalate if continues
  - group alerts by cause_tag (oom|driver|network) and suppress duplicates per-cause
Rob: That sounds reasonable. We should also consider a sliding threshold that accounts for node churn during rolling maintenance windows so we don't page for expected drift.
Daniel: Quick promql draft for "sustained" condition:
```
count_over_time(gpu.node.flare_count{region="us-west-2"}[5m]) > 2
```
Use `increase(...)` if events are counters.
Priya: Also recommend per-region quiet-hours window (local 22:00-07:00) that biases new noisy alerts to tickets instead of pages for non-prod clusters. For prod, keep stricter.
Rob: Can we route a percentage of suppressed pages to oncall (20%) and the rest to ticket queue so we can measure impact? an experiment tag on the alert rules would help.
Anya: Yep — plan: create a new rule `gpu-flare-probabilistic` in staging with a `experiment=quiet-burst-v1` label, and add a Grafana panel to show paged vs ticketed counts and the suppression rate.
sre-bot: deployment: alert rule 'gpu-flare-probabilistic' created in staging by Anya
Daniel: Minor tweak to the promql — prefer increase(gpu.node.flare_count[5m]) > 1 to capture event counts when metric is a counter. Also add `by(cause_tag)` to grouping so we can suppress per-cause.
Priya: Edge-case note: network partition can create many transient node errors. For that class, I suggest immediate ticket creation but no page unless host-level anomaly rate > 5% across the AZ. We'll add an explicit exception in the runbook.
Rob: Sounds good. Can someone open the PR with the Prometheus rule, the grafana panel JSON, and a short runbook note? I'll review and help with rollout gating.
Anya: On it — will open PR in ~1h and tag @Rob @Priya. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: incident-bot: oncall notified (Rob)
Priya: Also, add a dashboard chart `alert_noise_rate` that plots alerts_total / pages_total per 1h window so we can track whether suppression reduces noise without increasing time-to-detect.
Anya: We'll monitor SLO impact (median latency + error-rate) and have an automatic rollback trigger if user-facing error rate rises.
Rob: 👍 let's iterate; good first step away from immediate pages for every micro-flare.
